CREATIVE ARTS — TERMLY EXAM #18 (TERM 3)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. In a prone float, you keep your body (1 mark)
   A. stiff and bent
   B. curled with head up
   C. standing
   D. long and relaxed with face in the water

2. Where should you walk beside the pool? (1 mark)
   A. Jumping
   B. Running
   C. On the pool side, walking slowly
   D. Sliding

3. If someone is drowning, the safest action for a child is to (1 mark)
   A. jump in to save them
   B. run away silently
   C. laugh
   D. shout for an adult and throw something that floats

4. How should you use steps or a ladder to enter? (1 mark)
   A. Face the steps, hold the rails and go feet first
   B. Ignore rails
   C. Jump onto them
   D. Go head first

5. Which Kiswahili word means frog? (1 mark)
   A. chura
   B. tembo
   C. kaa
   D. twiga

6. Animal games improve (1 mark)
   A. only singing
   B. fitness and health
   C. only reading
   D. only cooking

7. In the hawk and the chicks game, the hen (1 mark)
   A. sits down
   B. tags everyone
   C. chases the hawk away for ever
   D. protects the chicks

8. Which game builds strong arms and shoulders as you crawl on hands and toes? (1 mark)
   A. Elephant walk
   B. Snake slither
   C. Giraffe stretch
   D. Crocodile crawl

9. Monkey swing helps to develop (1 mark)
   A. only hearing
   B. balance and coordination
   C. only counting
   D. only reading

10. The elephant walk stretches the (1 mark)
   A. back and the back of the legs
   B. ears
   C. tongue
   D. nose

11. In the frog jump, you begin (1 mark)
   A. standing on one leg
   B. in a squat with your hands on the ground
   C. sitting
   D. lying flat

12. Indigenous games are (1 mark)
   A. games from space
   B. traditional games that belong to a people and place
   C. games with no rules
   D. games played only with computers

13. A working portfolio holds (1 mark)
   A. food
   B. only finished prize work
   C. work in progress such as sketches and trials
   D. balls

14. Which words describe how loud or soft a performance was? (1 mark)
   A. Pitch
   B. Tempo
   C. Dynamics
   D. Diction

15. The Kenya National Anthem is called (1 mark)
   A. Malaika
   B. Twinkle Twinkle Little Star
   C. Jambo Bwana
   D. Ee Mungu Nguvu Yetu

16. Which material can you use to make a portfolio? (1 mark)
   A. Manila paper or cardboard
   B. Sand
   C. Glass
   D. Iron sheets

17. When presenting your artwork, you should hold it (1 mark)
   A. upside down
   B. by the middle with wet hands
   C. by one corner and shake
   D. carefully by the edges

18. Which is an example of appropriate behaviour when viewing a display? (1 mark)
   A. Being quiet and respectful
   B. Touching wet paint
   C. Laughing at others
   D. Running

19. What is used to close a homemade portfolio? (1 mark)
   A. A string or ribbon tie
   B. A padlock
   C. Wet glue only
   D. Nails

20. Sportsmanship means (1 mark)
   A. cheating to win
   B. hitting
   C. teasing others
   D. being fair and kind in sports

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. How should you behave when the Kenya National Anthem is sung? (3 marks)

22. Describe how to do the frog jump. (3 marks)

23. Explain how to perform an animal game to a musical rhythm. (4 marks)

24. State four things to think about when analysing an art work. (4 marks)

25. State four things you would look for when appreciating a sports performance. (4 marks)

26. What are indigenous games? (2 marks)

27. Explain how to analyse a folk song performance using its components. (5 marks)

28. Explain what is meant by two stars and a wish in feedback. (3 marks)

29. Why do we use a streamlined shape when gliding? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — TERMLY EXAM #18 (TERM 3) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — long and relaxed with face in the water
   A long relaxed body floats better.

2. C — On the pool side, walking slowly
   Wet floors are slippery.

3. D — shout for an adult and throw something that floats
   Do not enter the water; get help and throw a floating object.

4. A — Face the steps, hold the rails and go feet first
   Use the rails and enter carefully.

5. A — chura
   Chura is a frog.

6. B — fitness and health
   They strengthen muscles and improve stamina.

7. D — protects the chicks
   The hen blocks the hawk.

8. D — Crocodile crawl
   Body held straight on hands and toes.

9. B — balance and coordination
   Moving side to side lightly needs balance.

10. A — back and the back of the legs
   Bending forward stretches those muscles.

11. B — in a squat with your hands on the ground
   You squat and spring forward.

12. B — traditional games that belong to a people and place
   They are passed on by playing together.

13. C — work in progress such as sketches and trials
   It shows how work develops.

14. C — Dynamics
   Dynamics are loud and soft.

15. D — Ee Mungu Nguvu Yetu
   The Kiswahili title is Ee Mungu Nguvu Yetu.

16. A — Manila paper or cardboard
   Manila paper folds easily.

17. D — carefully by the edges
   Careful handling keeps it clean.

18. A — Being quiet and respectful
   Respect for others' work is important.

19. A — A string or ribbon tie
   Punched holes with string keep it closed.

20. D — being fair and kind in sports
   It includes following rules and respecting others.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: Stand straight and still, face the flag, remove your cap, sing clearly and do not talk or play.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: Squat with hands on the ground. Spring forward with the legs. Land softly on toes and hands with bent knees.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

23. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a game and a rhythm, clap or drum the beat, move to the beat, change the speed for different animals and add a song.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

24. (4 marks)
   Answer: Aesthetic, skills, message and behaviour. Feedback is also accepted.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

25. (4 marks)
   Answer: Teamwork, skill, safety and sportsmanship.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

26. (2 marks)
   Answer: Traditional games that belong to a people and were passed on from long ago.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

27. (5 marks)
   Answer: Say the community of origin, the type or occasion, the message and mood, the roles of the soloist, chorus and instrumentalists, and the instruments used.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of five components.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: Say two good things about the work and then give one suggestion for improvement.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: A long, thin shape slips through the water easily, so you glide further.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.
